Here's my take on the reason why mods of subverses can be power hungry.

I liken creating your own subverse to creating your own public garden. You cultivate and grow plants, specific plants that people enjoy looking at. You take time out every to day walk out, water and fertislise them to keep it fresh, on your own back.

Eventually these plants are fully grown and people have taken an interest to your garden, to your delight of course. People come, look around at the beauty of your plants and take fruit from them. At this point, your job is no longer to grow plants, it's to make sure the leaves are trimmed and to remove any weeds that might be littered around to keep them pristine. You grew the plants and now you maintain them, you have a sense of ownership.

After a while you decide you want other plants to be included in your garden, or the weeds are growing too quickly, or too much fruit is being taken, or people visitng are blocking the way for new visitors. You take measures, you remove some of the old plants, use stronger weed killer, put a sign up that requests people only take 1 fruit, and widen the entrance to allow plenty of people to come and join in.

However, the people who have visited your garden frequently don't like the changes. They feel like the fruit they have taken before has been small in number, that the stronger weed killer is damaging the plants and fruit, and that the old plants were fine. They feel the new people are taking subtracting from what your garden once was.

You don't agree. You want to make changes the people who regularly visted never wanted. You know it could be a good thing for the garden. Your regular visitors want things back the way they were.

You might react in different ways, you could allow the frequent visitors to your garden to vote the strength of the weed killer, or the amount of fruit that can be taken. Or, you could make the decision yourself as someone who has tended to the garden, who had the original vision and has been here since the beginning.

Very often, it takes a lot to get people to regularly visit your subs. Letting people know that your sub exists and then actually instilling content into the sub are some of the first neccisary steps to get it rolling. They don't usually take off without some dedicated interaction in the sub.

When the ball starts rolling and the most of the content is generated by users, you are doing less of the frame work, and more management work, making sure everything runs smoothly. That feeling of ownership you have could never just dissapear, it's why you typically get a lot of head mods saying 'This is my sub'.

It's tricky. There is a fine point where that sub no longer belongs the moderators, and they fade into the background. I can imagine the sub owners still want to be relevent, so they enforce their rules and beliefs onto the sub as a way of keeping ownership. Somtimes neccisary, sometimes not. Someone coming in from the outside wouldn't understand the time and effort the mod has gone through to cultivate and grow the community.

Here's what I personally think; Voat is in a state where users are flowing quickly and subs are small scale. You can easily make a sub here gaining traction very quickly, while on other sites such as Reddit, you're drown out by other subs. At this stage most subverses should belong to the communities, not a single or set of mods. Mods, you should take pride in the communities you fostered and listen to what they want, they come time and time again for the content they love, not the content you want.

TL;DR: Ownership and pride are a bitch for mods to deal with, and something users need to understand. Don't attribute their decisions with malice.
